% Generated by tools/impose.py -- do not edit.
%
% Cut into quarters, stack in order, sew along the spine edge.
%
% 8 book pages -> 1 sheets of US Letter, printed
% double-sided, flipped on the LONG edge.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[letterpaper,margin=0pt]{geometry}
\usepackage{pdfpages}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usepackage{xcolor}
\pagestyle{empty}

% Where to cut. Two pages across 8.5in leaves 3/4in of waste at each
% side, so the vertical cuts fall at 0.75in, 4.25in and 7.75in; two
% pages down is 11in exactly, so the only horizontal cut is the middle
% one and the top and bottom edges are the paper's own.
%
% Drawn here rather than with pdfpages' own frame option, which is a
% black hairline with no way to soften it. Matched to the book's hairline
% grey: a third of a point at 3.95:1, which a laser prints faithfully and
% which is still light enough that a remnant of it after an imperfect cut
% does not read as a border. The first attempt at 9A9A9A looked right on
% screen and needed good light to follow on paper.
\definecolor{cutline}{HTML}{7E7E7E}
\newcommand{\cutlines}{%
  \begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
    \foreach \cutx in {0.75, 4.25, 7.75} {%
      \draw[cutline, line width=0.3pt]
        ([xshift=\cutx in]current page.north west) --
        ([xshift=\cutx in]current page.south west);}
    \draw[cutline, line width=0.3pt]
      ([xshift=0.75in, yshift=-5.5in]current page.north west) --
      ([xshift=7.75in, yshift=-5.5in]current page.north west);
  \end{tikzpicture}}
\AddToHook{shipout/background}{\cutlines}

\begin{document}
\includepdf[
  pages={1,3,5,7,4,2,8,6},
  nup=2x2,
  noautoscale=true,
  delta=0pt 0pt,
  frame=false,
  turn=false,
]{screen-bass.pdf}
\end{document}
